A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Potential Score Matching work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite reflow, renumbering, and replacement of Figure 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original LJ-13/LJ-55 and MD17/MD22 sampling results, biased-training ablations, and time-dependent network diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 retains the original molecular sampling results and adds an aspirin timing experiment and 1D/2D synthetic sampling results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the force-based objective, Piecewise and Piecewise Weighted losses, and time-conditioned Equiformer-v2 remain unchanged. The revised time-embedding description concerns an existing component; Euler sampling was already supported in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds 1D bimodal and 2D ring-shaped synthetic sampling tasks. Existing LJ-13/LJ-55 and MD17/MD22 molecular coverage is retained; aspirin was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an evaluated QuinNet-based molecular-dynamics comparator for the aspirin timing experiment. Existing comparisons with FAB, iDEM, and DSM retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new timing experiment specifies 500 PSM training epochs, Euler sampling, 1,000 batches with 1,000 timesteps each, and 210,000 MD steps. Tables 6-7 retain the existing benchmark splits, budgets, noise schedules, and predictor-corrector sampling settings.

E4.justification: The supplementary analysis suite changes substantially: v2 adds computational-cost analysis and standalone-PSM versus hybrid-loss toy tests, while removing v1 Figure 6's molecular network-versus-target and label-dispersion diagnostics. This changes the evidence examining efficiency and when force labels suffice. The ethanol training-bias ablation remains.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains its three sampling seeds and uncertainty reporting, and Table 6 retains seed 42. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 and Figure 4's SOAP cluster percentages are unchanged. New timing results report approximately 8 hours training and 10 minutes sampling for PSM, versus 24 hours and 31 hours 18 minutes for MD under their respective workloads. Toy-distribution findings are added, and the earlier time-dependent diagnostic results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit proof of Lemma 1 while retaining its statement. New Appendix B.2 makes the noise-loss relationship explicit but largely repeats score and reconstruction-loss derivations already present in v1. The principal theorems and their assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about force-label debiasing, small-time score accuracy and variance, efficient sampling, and applicability to high-dimensional molecular systems.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of weakened force-label constraints at large noise times and removes v1's empirical recommendation against a PSM cutoff above 0.2. The SOAP discussion also reframes the unchanged training mixture as deliberately introducing controlled bias.

D1.justification: v2 adds single-A100 hardware disclosure, timing-experiment details, and toy-density/force specifications. The Figure 4 discussion drops its explicit evaluation sample counts. Existing hyperparameter tables and data-access links remain unchanged; the new toy density and force have inconsistent signs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to QuinNet and Vincent's denoising-score-matching work. Sections 3 and B.4 expand the positioning relative to TSM, including architectural contrasts with energy-based MLPs and attribution of the Gaussian variance-proof strategy.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify score-matching background, loss notation, and the SOAP experiment. v2 adds a loss-relationships subsection and ablation subheadings, removes the contents page, and updates the author list with Tao Qin. Most narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is replaced by a multi-panel toy-distribution comparison. The unchanged Figure 7 moves from a standalone final page into the appendix text, Tables 6-7 are redistributed, and the author block is compacted. Other principal displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The added timing measurements and explanations are useful, but v2 removes the earlier time-dependent molecular diagnostics. The timing study does not quantify matched sampling accuracy, and the new toy density exp(-5||x||^2+||x||^4) has a log-gradient opposite to the stated force label (Appendix C/Figure 6). These competing changes, with the main results unchanged, leave the net quality direction uncertain.
